_comment: WHAT THIS PASS WAS FOR. Two things: find out why the Electron arm draws
panes the shared default layout does not place (PARITY-S1/S14), and close
the editor row-pitch gap whose direction had flipped (PARITY-S5).
THE HEADLINE. PARITY-S1 WAS NOT A PRODUCT FINDING. It was the output
directory. The Electron lane graded whatever `<view>.png` and
`<view>.capture.json` were on disk, and three of the six scenarios had
failed before their capture step, leaving the 2026-10-12 run's frames in
place — frames taken five days before the `noUserLayout` fixture option
and therefore showing the raw bundled tree's TEST RESULTS / CONSTRAINTS
column. The records say so themselves: `takenAt` 2026-10-12T20:29..20:39Z
on exactly the three views that reported seven panes, against
2026-10-17T13:19..13:25Z on the three that did not.
EVERY FINDING SAYS WHETHER IT WAS RE-MEASURED OR INHERITED
(`measuredThisPass`), and every claim names the commit it was measured
STANDING: HOST-CONDITIONAL EVIDENCE, NEVER A REQUIRED GATE. Both lanes
need a live macOS GUI session and a kTCCServiceScreenCapture grant.
Raw per-frame records are in build/plat37-parity-2026-10-18/ (gitignored).

theStaleFrameFinding.question: Is Electron right or wrong to draw TESTS and CONSTRAINTS where the shared default places neither?
theStaleFrameFinding.answer: NEITHER. The build under test never drew them. The reading came from three frames the 2026-10-17 run did not take.
theStaleFrameFinding.whichOfTheThreeCandidates: CANDIDATE 1, in a sharpened form. Not the test fixture leaking state BETWEEN SCENARIOS — the launch fixture's `noUserLayout: true` is set once for every scenario in the spec's loop (plat37-electron-window-capture.spec.ts:658) and `removeUserLayout()` runs before every launch. It is the OUTPUT DIRECTORY leaking frames BETWEEN RUNS.
theEvidenceThatDecided: TWO INDEPENDENT TIMESTAMPS AGREE, PER VIEW. The capture driver stamps each record with `takenAt`, and the filesystem stamps each PNG. Read 2026-10-18 out of build/plat37-macos-electron/, left over from the run graded against codetracer 596cb6e50: state takenAt 2026-10-12T20:32:36Z / png mtime 2026-10-12T20:32:39Z; calltrace 20:39:06Z / 20:39:09Z; editor 20:29:47Z / 20:29:50Z; eventLog 2026-10-17T13:23:08Z / 13:23:11Z; editorWithMark 13:25:20Z / 13:25:23Z; shell 13:19:34Z / 13:19:43Z. Each pair agrees to within the 3-9 s a capture takes.

THE SPLIT IS EXACTLY THE FINDING'S SPLIT. The three views with 2026-10-12 stamps — state, calltrace, editor — are precisely the three the 2026-10-17 pass reported as drawing SEVEN panes with a TESTS / CONSTRAINTS column. The three with 2026-10-17 stamps are the ones that reported five, five and four. The correlation is one-to-one over six rows.

THE GEOMETRY CORROBORATES, ARITHMETICALLY, AND THE TWO FRAMES MATCH TWO DIFFERENT FILES. The FRESH editorWithMark frame's Electron columns at the 1440-point viewport are 289 / 357 / 787 points of 1433 (two 4-point splitters make up the 1440) = 20.17% / 24.91% / 54.92%, against the generated oracle's 20 / 25 / 55 — every column within 0.2 points. The STALE state frame's are 218 / 355 / 585 / 270 of 1428 (three splitters) = 15.27% / 24.86% / 40.97% / 18.91%, against the RAW BUNDLED tree's 20 / 55 / 25 each scaled by 0.75 with a 25% editor inserted = 15.00 / 25.00 / 41.25 / 18.75 — every column within 0.3 points. Two frames, two different layout files, each matched to a fraction of a point. The bundled tree has no editor slot at all (its ten components are filesystem, vCS, state, scratchpad, calltrace, agentActivity, eventLog, terminal, testResults, constraints), which is why the editor's 25% has to be inserted and the rest rescaled.

THE DATES BRACKET THE FIX. `noUserLayout: true` entered this lane's spec in 9226bc5ed (2026-10-15T16:40). Every stale frame predates it; every fresh frame postdates it. The 2026-10-14 fix DID work — it was never re-measured on three of the six views.
theStaleFrameFinding.soTheOracleIsNotIncomplete: The second candidate — 'Electron legitimately opens these panes and the shared default does not describe them, so GPUI is the deficient side' — is REFUTED, and by the product's own code rather than only by the frames. `src/config/default_layout.json` and `src/frontend/headless_app/shared_default_layout.generated.json` are BOTH written by one generator (`headless_app/generate_default_layout.nim`) from one input: the first is the bundled tree, the second is that tree through `index/mode_default_layout.modeDefaultLayout(_, DebugMode)`. The bundled tree gives TEST RESULTS and CONSTRAINTS a column of their own on purpose, and the mode derivation removes them. `index/config.installModeDefault` applies that derivation on first run and on View > Reset Layout, and its own comment records that copying the bundled file verbatim — which is what it did until 2026-09-27 — is the defect that produced 'a standing TEST RESULTS / CONSTRAINTS column that no mode draws'. The oracle is complete; the frames were old.
theStaleFrameFinding.andTheThirdCandidate: 'The capture samples before the layout settles' is not what produced the seven-pane census either, because the frames in question were not sampled at all in that run. It remains live for PARITY-S14 and for PARITY-I1's `editorSettledBetweenOperations`, which are separate.
theStaleFrameFinding.andOneGateSaysItOUTRIGHT: ci/test/default-layout-fresh.sh regenerates BOTH src/config/default_layout.json and src/frontend/headless_app/shared_default_layout.generated.json from the single generator and fails if either differs by one byte. So 'the bundled tree and the shared default are one computation, not two that happen to agree' is not an inference from reading the generator — it is a gate, and this pass ran it (see `freshnessGates.defaultLayoutFresh`).

THAT SUMMARY IS WRONG: only ONE of the four is that assertion.

theRowPitchFinding.question: GPUI 22.0-22.5 points against Electron 23.5-24.5 at codetracer 596cb6e50 — GPUI the tighter, where it had been the looser. Where is the pitch decided, and can GPUI derive it rather than copy it?
theRowPitchFinding.answer: GPUI was carrying MONACO'S LINUX ANSWER as a literal on a macOS host. It is now derived, and the derivation is Monaco's own rule.
theMechanism: The desktop never sets Monaco's `lineHeight`. `editor.nim`'s `createMonacoEditor` call (src/frontend/ui/editor.nim:3245-3270) passes `fontSize` and `fontFamily` and no `lineHeight`, so the option stays at `EDITOR_FONT_DEFAULTS.lineHeight`, which is 0 (editorOptions.js:2917) — Monaco's 'compute it from the font size' branch.

That branch is PLATFORM-DEPENDENT. In the Monaco this product ships, `node_modules/monaco-editor/esm/vs/editor/common/config/fontInfo.js:12` reads `export const GOLDEN_LINE_HEIGHT_RATIO = platform.isMacintosh ? 1.5 : 1.35;` and line 36 `lineHeight = GOLDEN_LINE_HEIGHT_RATIO * fontSize;`, rounded at line 42.

The font size is 16 on both arms: the desktop's `data.ui.fontSize` (frontend/utils.nim:1039) which it hands Monaco, and the GPUI front-end's own default (app/leaves.nim's `if sizePx != 16`, 16 being the size it does not bother to set).

So Monaco draws round(1.35 * 16) = 22 on Linux and round(1.5 * 16) = 24 on macOS. `chrome.EditorLinePx` was the literal `22` — correct on Linux, two points short on macOS, and the gap the instrument measured.

whatWasChanged.what: `EditorLinePx` is now `monacoLineHeightPx(CodeFontPx)`. `monacoLineHeightPx` transcribes `BareFontInfo._create`'s four lines — the automatic branch, the em branch for an option below 8, the absolute branch, the round, and the 8 px floor — and `MonacoGoldenLineHeightRatio` is `when defined(macosx): 1.5 else: 1.35`, the same conditional Monaco writes. `CodeFontPx = 16` names the one font size both front-ends use.
whatWasChanged.whyADerivationAndNotTheConstant24: A literal cannot be right on both platforms, and the Linux arm of this campaign measures the same finding against Monaco's 22. The derivation is right on both and moves by itself if the font size ever does. The editor-zoom multiplier is deliberately NOT transcribed: this front-end has no zoom control, so copying `EditorZoom.getZoomLevel()` would invent a second answer for a level that is always 0.
whatWasChanged.alsoUpdated: The three comments that still spelled the literal 22 — `window_geometry.GpuiEditorRowPx`, `app/leaves.renderEditorRow`, and `tests/test_plat47_window_gestures.nim` — now say what the derivation gives on each platform.

instrumentControls._rule: A uniform result across all rows is a broken probe until proven otherwise. Each entry says what the probe answered DIFFERENTLY, and on what.
instrumentControls.theDerivedPitchConstant: POSITIVE CONTROL, and not uniform. build/plat37-parity-2026-10-18/showpitch.nim imports the REAL `gpui/chrome` and prints the derivation's branches: EditorLinePx 24, monacoLineHeightPx(16) 24, (12) 18, (16,2) 32 (the em branch), (16,30) 30 (the absolute branch), (1) 8 (the floor). Five inputs, five different answers, each the one Monaco's `BareFontInfo._create` gives. MonacoGoldenLineHeightRatio printed 1.5, which is the macOS arm of the `when`.
instrumentControls.theStaleFrameGuard: POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE CONTROL, over the exact comparison the lane now makes, on three synthetic records: `takenAt` 2026-10-12T20:32:36Z (the real stale value) -> REFUSED; 2026-10-17T13:25:20Z (the real fresh value) -> graded; no `takenAt` at all -> REFUSED. Three rows, two outcomes, so the guard is not answering one thing to everything.
instrumentControls.theRowPitchInstrument: UNCHANGED from the 2026-10-17 pass and deliberately so, because it is the before/after instrument: the MODE of consecutive `lineBands` centre deltas at 0.5-point resolution, a statistic of the oracle's ink projection using no OCR at all. The gutter-digit estimator was already rejected by that pass for reading 15-22 usable steps per GPUI frame against 0-2 per Electron frame. Its own liveness control is that it does NOT answer uniformly: see the before table, where it reads 22.0 and 22.5 on GPUI and 23.5, 24.0 and 24.5 on Electron, with support between 6 and 17 deltas.
instrumentControls.theTypecheckOnTheSpecChange: POSITIVE CONTROL. `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` over src/tests/gui reports 14 errors, all in four unrelated specs (auto-hide-panes, omniscience_eye_icon, m24-session-toml-load, python-trivial-chain) and none in the edited file. To show tsc actually reads the edited file, `readEditorFontMetrics` was renamed to `readEditorFontMetricsTYPO` at its call site and the run then reported `plat37-electron-window-capture.spec.ts(824,34): error TS2552: Cannot find name 'readEditorFontMetricsTYPO'`. The file was restored and re-checked.
instrumentControls.theShellScriptChange: `bash -n` and `shellcheck -S warning` both exit 0 on the edited ci/test/plat37-macos-electron-capture.sh.
instrumentControls.flipdiffProvenance: REUSED, the binary built 2026-10-12 at build/plat37-parity/flipdiff, as the 2026-10-17 pass did. Justified by measurement, and stated precisely: it was built from codetracer-image-diff ee9fb397b and `git -C codetracer-image-diff rev-parse HEAD` still reads ee9fb397b94155557d730ee6997db60687214988, so the FLIP implementation in the binary is byte-identical to THIS CHECKOUT's. The REMOTE moved to 5a4a6e792 during the pass (see `upstreamRecheckedAtTheEnd`); the binary is the checkout's revision, not the remote's.
instrumentControls.structdumpProvenance: REUSED, the binary built 2026-10-17T16:28 from build/plat37-parity-2026-10-17/structdump.nim. Justified by measurement: `git diff --name-only 596cb6e50..d883db0e2 -- src/tests/visual/screen_oracle` is EMPTY, and structdump.nim itself was copied unchanged, so neither the probe nor the oracle primitives it links moved between the two subjects.

new.title: The PLAT-37 Electron capture lane grades frames it did not take
new.measured: ci/test/plat37-macos-electron-capture.sh's grading loop tested only `[ -f "${rec}" ]`. The capture happens inside Playwright, in a separate process, before the loop runs, so a scenario whose test died before its capture step left the PREVIOUS run's PNG and record in the output directory and the loop graded them. Against codetracer 596cb6e50 on 2026-10-17 this made three of six views report a pane census taken on 2026-10-12, which was recorded and reasoned about as PARITY-S1, 'Electron draws seven panes where the shared default places five', for five days across three readings files.
new.whyTheGpuiLaneIsImmune: plat37-macos-window-capture.sh:496 does `rm -f "${png}" "${points_png}" "${rec}" "${grade}" "${log}"` immediately before it launches the window and captures, so a view it fails to capture has NO record and is counted a refusal. The asymmetry is the defect.
new.remedyApplied: A run stamp. The lane records `RUN_STARTED_AT` (`date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`, the same spelling the driver writes into `takenAt`) before the Playwright drive, and refuses any record whose `takenAt` is absent or lexicographically earlier, naming both timestamps. The stale artefact is KEPT, because it is the evidence that something went wrong; it is simply not graded.
new.severity: high — it silently attributes an old build's rendering to the build under test, in a lane whose entire output is attributions of that kind

new.title: The PLAT-37 Electron capture lane never set CODETRACER_PERF_LIMIT_SCALE
new.measured: `lib/performance-limits.ts`'s docstring says the knob exists for lanes whose subject is not performance and names the visual captures; the sibling PLAT-35 Electron lane has set it since its first run (Justfile:5012, default 4). The PLAT-37 lane set nothing, so `LIMIT_FIRST_WINDOW_MS` stayed at 10 s. Against codetracer 596cb6e50 on 2026-10-17, on a host at load average ~13, `advanced-state` and `returned-calltrace` both died inside the LAUNCH fixture with `Performance limit exceeded: "first window" took 35567ms / 32122ms (limit: 10000ms)` — two of the four failures, and two of the three views that then got a stale frame graded in their place.
new.remedyApplied: `export CODETRACER_PERF_LIMIT_SCALE="${CODETRACER_PERF_LIMIT_SCALE:-6}"` in the lane. 6 and not the sibling's 4 because 35567 ms is 89% of the 40 s a scale of 4 gives, which `timed` itself prints as SLOW.
new.severity: medium — it turns host contention into a capture failure, and before unfiled-A that capture failure turned into a false product finding

new.title: corpus-pins.json pins editor row counts that are platform-dependent by construction
new.measured: `src/tests/visual/corpus-pins.json` pins `gpuiEditorRows` and `electronEditorRows` as exact admissible-string sets (`rows=45;first=1;last=45`), and `test_cross_renderer_visual_alignment.nim:854` asserts set membership with no tolerance. But the row count is the pane height over Monaco's line height, and Monaco's line height is `GOLDEN_LINE_HEIGHT_RATIO * fontSize` with the ratio 1.5 on macOS and 1.35 elsewhere (fontInfo.js:12). At font size 16 that is 24 px against 22 px, so the SAME pane holds a different number of rows on the two platforms and no single pinned string can be right on both.
new.suggestedRemedy: Either scope the pinned arrays per platform, or add the macOS answers to the existing arrays — the file's own comment already establishes the array as an admissible SET rather than a single value, and `pinnedRowsAreDefended` already requires a reason for a multi-member set, which this is.
new.notDoneHere: No pin was edited. The pins were re-pinned twice on 2026-10-17 by the Linux arm of this campaign and re-pinning them from a macOS run would make that arm's readings wrong.
new.severity: medium — it will redden the cross-renderer gate on macOS the first time anyone runs it there

new.title: The 2026-10-17 readings misreport all four Electron Playwright failures as one assertion
new.measured: `plat37-parity-readings-2026-10-17.json`'s `laneOutcomes.electron.playwright` says 'All four failures are the same assertion at plat37-electron-window-capture.spec.ts:862, `the editor drew no rows`'. The run's own playwright.log shows ONE of the four is that assertion (entry-shell); two are `Performance limit exceeded: "first window"` thrown in the launch fixture and one is `the 'stepIn' toolbar button (#step-in-image) is not in the DOM` thrown in `drive`.
new.whyItMattered: The misreport is what made the three stale frames look like captures that had happened and then failed a DOM assertion, rather than captures that never happened at all. It is corrected in this file.
new.severity: low as a defect, high as a lesson — a reporter's summary line was read in place of the log

rowPitchBeforeAndAfter.unit: points. The statistic is the MODE of consecutive lineBands centre deltas at 0.5-point resolution — no OCR.

rowPitchBeforeAndAfter.summary: GPUI moved 22.0-22.5 -> 24.0-24.5 on every one of the six frames. ELECTRON DID NOT MOVE ON ANY OF THE FIVE WHERE BOTH PASSES MEASURED IT: 23.5 / 24.0 / 24.5 / 24.5 / 24.0, the same five values. The per-view gap went from 1.5-2.5 points to 0.0-0.5.
rowPitchBeforeAndAfter.theREFERENCEvalue: 24 px at font size 16, read from Monaco itself on all six fresh Electron route records (`editorFontMetrics.lineHeightPx`), not inferred from ink.
rowPitchBeforeAndAfter.whyTHEinstrumentSTILLreads23_5onONEframe: state's Electron mode is 23.5 with only 6 supporting deltas out of 36, and its median is 23.5 too, while Monaco says 24. The ink estimator carries about half a point of quantisation on ELECTRON frames specifically — Monaco positions and antialiases glyphs sub-pixel, so band centroids scatter — and essentially none on GPUI frames, which read exactly 24.0 where the code draws 24. That is the reason this pass added the direct Monaco read: the estimator was good enough to find a 2-point error and is not good enough to certify a half-point one.
rowPitchBeforeAndAfter.bandCounts: GPUI 37/37/37/45/44/47 -> 35/34/34/40/40/43 (state/calltrace/editorWithMark/editor/eventLog/shell), the predicted consequence of a taller row in the same pane. Electron 37/37/38/47/43/- -> 37/37/38/47/43/46, unchanged wherever it was measured before.
